purpose: Write down every authentication pathway in the tree, with the controls and the authentication strength behind each, as ASVS 5.0 V6.1.3 requires, and hold the list to the code with a test so it cannot go stale. Documentation and a test only. No runtime behaviour changes, no route is added, removed or re-gated, and no production deploy.
requiredInvariants: No runtime code changes at all. Not one file under apps/ is touched: no route is added, removed, re-gated or re-scoped, and no control is loosened. The pass establishes what is there, it does not change it.

The inventory was built by measuring the tree, not by reading the previous record. Every file that signs a session token or writes a session cookie was enumerated; the survey found twelve, of which the previous evidence named one - and that one, the gov-id bridge, mints nothing.

No pathway found is claimed to be a defect. All twelve are controlled and no open door was found; the finding is that the security record did not know five of them existed, which is precisely what V6.1.3 governs.

The workflow edit only widens when an existing gate runs. Two path entries are added to sbom-scan.yml so an edit to THREAT_MODEL.md or to the new test triggers the job that runs it. No gate is weakened, no check is removed, and no step is skipped.

V6.1.3 moves to PASS on a document only because the document is enforced. The test enumerates every minting surface and fails when one is unaccounted for, and fails again when a named pathway leaves the document; the ASVS condition is PRESENT_ALL_AT_PATH over the pathway names, so dropping one from the document revokes the decision rather than leaving a stale PASS.

V6.3.4 deliberately stays FAIL. Its first half - no undocumented pathways - is now met, but the second half asks that controls and strength be enforced CONSISTENTLY across all twelve surfaces, which needs per-surface evidence about what the middleware trusts a cabinet cookie to assert. That is not proven and is not claimed.
No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. The 1C, marketing and presentation contours are not touched.
acceptance: The pathway test passes 5 of 5 and both mutations are caught: an undocumented minting surface added to apps/ fails it, and removing a documented pathway from THREAT_MODEL.md fails it.
The matrix rebuilds at applied 332 / rejected 0: PASS 102 to 103, FAIL 117 to 116, NOT_ASSESSED unchanged at 38.
Removing one pathway name from THREAT_MODEL.md revokes V6.1.3 at the matrix level - applied 331 / rejected 1, PASS back to 102 - so the PASS is held by the condition rather than asserted.
